title: Navigating Pensions for Psychologists and Mental Health Professionals

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到除了用时间换金钱之外的收入，那会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，自 2019 年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要告诉大家。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: Sophie Foote 的“一对多”（One-to-Many）项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员计划和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己曾在 2022 年完成了这个项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的转型之旅。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得 Sophie 的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四场小组大师班、大师课、个性化指导、一份 Fortnum and Mason 的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名截止时间为 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 请通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。

sentences.en: Coming up in today's episode, are you ready to unravel the secrets of pensions as a mental health professional and inspiring psychologist?
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，作为一名心理健康专业人士和有抱负的心理学家，你准备好揭开养老金的秘密了吗？

sentences.en: Join us in this very special episode where I'm joined by a qualified independent financial advisor where we go through all things pension.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听这期非常特别的节目，我邀请了一位合格的独立财务顾问，我们将深入探讨养老金的所有相关事宜。

sentences.en: Loads of great advice in there and answering all of your questions.
sentences.zh: 节目中有很多很棒的建议，并会回答你们所有的问题。

sentences.en: Tune in and equip yourself with all of the skills, advice and strategy you need to be liberated in your financial freedom in future.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，掌握你未来实现财务自由所需的技能、建议和策略。

sentences.en: Hope you find it so useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这期节目很有用。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到《有抱负的心理学家》播客。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent and I'm a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是 Marianne Trent 博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Something I really struggled with when I was earlier in my career was feeling like a proper enough grown-up to take myself seriously and look at pensions.
sentences.zh: 我职业生涯早期真正挣扎的一件事是，觉得自己还不够成熟，无法认真对待自己并去考虑养老金问题。

sentences.en: It was something that was always on my to-do list but never really seemed like the right time.
sentences.zh: 这总是在我的待办事项清单上，但似乎从来都不是合适的时机。

sentences.en: I'm telling you now is the right time.
sentences.zh: 我现在告诉你，现在就是合适的时机。

sentences.en: But I know that can still feel tricky.
sentences.zh: 但我知道这仍然会让人觉得很棘手。

sentences.en: Previously for episode 76, I was joined by Ian Dempsey,
sentences.zh: 在之前的第 76 期节目中，我邀请了 Ian Dempsey，

sentences.en: an independent financial advisor and we were talking generally about money and trying to make ends meet and having it to stretch to cover our bases but also to kind of think about financial planning.
sentences.zh: 他是一位独立财务顾问，我们当时泛泛地谈论了金钱、如何维持生计、如何量入为出，同时也谈到了财务规划。

sentences.en: I've invited him back by special request where we're going to be looking specifically at pensions.
sentences.zh: 应特别要求，我再次邀请了他，这次我们将专门探讨养老金问题。

sentences.en: This is ideal if you are any kind of mental health professional and if you are a qualified or an unqualified member of staff.
sentences.zh: 如果你是任何类型的心理健康专业人士，无论你是合格还是非合格的员工，这期节目都非常适合你。

sentences.en: Let's dive in and meet Ian again and yeah, I will catch you on the other side.
sentences.zh: 让我们开始吧，再次见到 Ian，是的，稍后见。

sentences.en: Today we have Ian Dempsey with us who you might remember a few months back we were talking about all things money and we have a special request for Ian to come back and talk about pensions today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们请到了 Ian Dempsey，大家可能还记得几个月前我们谈论了所有关于金钱的话题，今天我们特别邀请 Ian 回来谈谈养老金。

sentences.en: Hi Ian, thank you for joining us.
sentences.zh: 嗨 Ian，谢谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: You're very welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: I mean, yes, come on back again.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，欢迎回来。

sentences.en: We should make it a regular start really, shouldn't we?
sentences.zh: 我们真的应该把它变成一个固定栏目，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think, yeah, I think so many of us don't really understand money that that's probably not a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的，我觉得我们很多人真的不懂钱，所以这可能不是个坏主意。

sentences.en: And I think part of the challenge we've got at the minute, as we just said off air, it's really challenging to look after your money at the moment, cost the living,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们目前面临的部分挑战是，正如我们刚才在节目外说的，现在打理钱财真的很有挑战性，生活成本，

sentences.en: investment markets aren't particularly well, interest rates are doing great guns at the moment, but that could be a double-edged sword with your mortgage going up.
sentences.zh: 投资市场表现不太好，利率目前很高，但这可能是一把双刃剑，因为你的抵押贷款成本也在上升。

sentences.en: But potentially you're getting a bigger return on your savings account.
sentences.zh: 但你可能会从储蓄账户中获得更高的回报。

sentences.en: It's like, I think I said to you, it's, I've been doing this for 17 years now and these economic conditions we're in right now are the worst I've seen in 17 years.
sentences.zh: 就像我之前对你说的，我做这一行已经 17 年了，我们现在所处的经济环境是我 17 年来见过的最糟糕的。

sentences.en: And it's just a real mix of emotion, challenge and circumstances.
sentences.zh: 这真的是情绪、挑战和环境的混合体。

sentences.en: It's tough.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: Like it's really, really hard to manage your money at the moment, I think right across the board, no matter what level of wealth or where you are in your career journey, it's hard.
sentences.zh: 我觉得目前管理钱财真的非常非常困难，无论你的财富水平如何，或者你处于职业生涯的哪个阶段，这都很难。

sentences.en: It's really, really tough.
sentences.zh: 真的非常非常艰难。

sentences.en: Yeah, I couldn't agree more.
sentences.zh: 是的，我完全同意。

sentences.en: I couldn't agree more.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意。

sentences.en: And I guess we just have to hope it will, you know, what we know about is it bull and bear years that we will get back up there again and things will improve.
sentences.zh: 我想我们只能希望，你知道，我们所知道的牛市和熊市，我们会再次回升，情况会好转。

sentences.en: I mean, it will a hundred percent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，百分之百会好转。

sentences.en: Like if you look at history and as much as the FCSA past performance isn't an indication of the future, every single time we go through this, it gets better.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看历史，尽管金融行为监管局（FCA）常说过去的表现不代表未来，但我们每次经历这种情况，情况都会好转。

sentences.en: It's just holding your nerve and staying consistent with your approach.
sentences.zh: 关键在于保持冷静，并坚持你的策略。

sentences.en: That's what makes a big difference long term.
sentences.zh: 这就是长期来看产生巨大差异的原因。

sentences.en: But that's easier said than done if maybe this is the time that you've just started.
sentences.zh: 但如果这恰好是你刚开始的时候，说起来容易做起来难。

sentences.en: And I think part of the challenge we've got is we've had good markets for 10 years, had good returns, solid returns for a long period of time while interest rates have been low.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们面临的部分挑战是，过去 10 年市场表现良好，在利率较低的长期时间内获得了稳健的回报。

sentences.en: So having conversations about investments and pensions has been a very, very easy conversation because you could just pull those figures out and just compare the two.
sentences.zh: 所以谈论投资和养老金一直是一个非常非常容易的话题，因为你可以直接拿出那些数据进行比较。

sentences.en: Now it's very, very different.
sentences.zh: 现在情况大不相同了。

sentences.en: And I've got clients in investments, as I kind of mentioned off air, that are just unsure whether it's the right thing for them.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才在节目外提到的，我有一些投资客户，他们只是不确定这是否适合他们。

sentences.en: Long term, 100% it is.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，百分之百是适合的。

sentences.en: But right now, is it the right thing?
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，这是正确的做法吗？

sentences.en: So there's some real challenges and some difficult conversations kind of happening behind the scenes at the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以目前幕后确实存在一些真正的挑战和艰难的对话。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, there are.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And it really does make me think about when I was in a position that was probably quite fortunate.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我想起我当时处于一个可能相当幸运的位置。

sentences.en: I won't, you know, I won't lie.
sentences.zh: 我不会，你知道，我不会撒谎。

sentences.en: When I was working full time as an assistant psychologist and I was living with my parents, I think I only paid about £100 a month rent.
sentences.zh: 当我全职担任助理心理学家并与父母住在一起时，我想我每月只需支付约 100 英镑的房租。

sentences.en: It was very, very low key.
sentences.zh: 那真的很低调。

sentences.en: And I really probably at that point was thinking, should I start a pension?
sentences.zh: 当时我可能真的在想，我应该开始存养老金吗？

sentences.en: Shouldn't I start a pension?
sentences.zh: 我不应该开始存养老金吗？

sentences.en: And I guess other people listening to this might well be having that similar feeling.
sentences.zh: 我想听节目的其他人可能也会有类似的感觉。

sentences.en: So I think I'm right in saying that if you're employed, you kind of have to be offered a workplace pension.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我说得没错，如果你是受雇员工，雇主通常必须为你提供工作场所养老金。

sentences.en: Is that right, Ian?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗，Ian？

sentences.en: It is, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So auto-enrollment came in a few years back, which effectively became a legal requirement for employers, initially of a certain size.
sentences.zh: 几年前引入了自动加入机制，这实际上成为了雇主的法律要求，最初是针对一定规模的企业。

sentences.en: And then it's just been phased out with smaller and smaller employers to offer a pension.
sentences.zh: 然后它逐渐推广到越来越小的雇主，要求他们提供养老金。

sentences.en: And the minimum contribution of that pension in total is 8%.
sentences.zh: 该养老金的最低缴费总额为 8%。

sentences.en: So that would be 5% from you, 3% from your employer.
sentences.zh: 也就是你出 5%，雇主出 3%。

sentences.en: But it's very easy for you to opt out of it.
sentences.zh: 但你很容易选择退出。

sentences.en: You could say, I don't want to be part of that pension.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，我不想参加那个养老金计划。

sentences.en: I don't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我不想做。

sentences.en: But it's when you're kind of young, free, and you've got the world at your feet, do you really think about a pension?
sentences.zh: 但是当你年轻、自由，世界就在你脚下时，你真的会考虑养老金吗？

sentences.en: No, you don't.
sentences.zh: 不，你不会。

sentences.en: I didn't.
sentences.zh: 我当时就没有。

sentences.en: And I'm just going to start a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 我只是打算晚一点再开始。

sentences.en: But I think in the 17 years I've been doing this, when I look at the experience of clients that have got to a really strong retirement position
sentences.zh: 但我认为在我从事这一行的 17 年里，当我看到那些在退休时处于非常稳固地位的客户的经历时，

sentences.en: or have got significant wealth built up for later on in life, they started early.
sentences.zh: 或者那些为晚年积累了大量财富的人，他们都是尽早开始的。

sentences.en: And they didn't start with massive amounts because that compound effect over a period of time just spirals and spirals and gets bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 他们开始时并没有投入巨额资金，因为复利效应在一段时间内会不断螺旋式上升，变得越来越大。

sentences.en: And those margins of contribution levels to growth get wider and wider every single time.
sentences.zh: 而且缴费水平与增长之间的差距每次都在扩大。

sentences.en: So start as soon as you possibly can, even if it's only just a relatively small amount.
sentences.zh: 所以尽可能早地开始，即使只是相对较小的金额。

sentences.en: It makes a big difference long term.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，这会产生很大的不同。

sentences.en: And ultimately, the way you've got to think about it in simple terms is if you put £100 in, your employer is going to top that up,
sentences.zh: 归根结底，简单来说，如果你投入 100 英镑，你的雇主会补足这笔钱，

sentences.en: then you're going to get your tax relief on top of that.
sentences.zh: 然后你还会获得税收减免。

sentences.en: Straight away off the bat, you've got well over a 30% to 40% uplift.
sentences.zh: 立刻，你就有超过 30% 到 40% 的收益提升。

sentences.en: If I could get clients 30%, 40% uplift on investments, I'd be retired by now because I'd be doing the same.
sentences.zh: 如果我能让客户在投资上获得 30% 到 40% 的提升，我现在早就退休了，因为我也会做同样的事情。

sentences.en: You know, that's an incredible free uplift to your savings or investments that you don't get on an ISA, you don't get on a savings account,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是对你储蓄或投资的一笔不可思议的免费提升，你在 ISA（个人储蓄账户）中得不到，在储蓄账户中也得不到，

sentences.en: you don't get deductions against your mortgage for that.
sentences.zh: 你也不能用它来抵扣抵押贷款。

sentences.en: Tax relief for 20% as a basic rate taxpayer, 40% at higher rates, plus an employer contribution is huge.
sentences.zh: 作为基本税率纳税人，20% 的税收减免，高税率下为 40%，加上雇主的缴费，这非常可观。

sentences.en: Make the most of it.
sentences.zh: 充分利用它。

sentences.en: Because if you don't, in simple terms, that money just stays with your employer.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你不这样做，简单来说，那笔钱就留在了你的雇主那里。

sentences.en: That just becomes their profit, does it?
sentences.zh: 那只是变成了他们的利润，是吗？

sentences.en: They just put that back into their own coffers.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把它放回了自己的金库。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And there's no obligation for them to do that if you've opted out of that scheme because you've made the decision.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你因为自己做出了决定而退出了该计划，他们没有义务为你做任何事。

sentences.en: You've decided, I don't want to be part of this scheme, therefore I'm going to step back.
sentences.zh: 你决定了，我不想参加这个计划，因此我要退出。

sentences.en: Some of the bigger companies will say, well, we'll give you an extra £150 a month on your salary or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 一些大公司会说，好吧，我们会在你的工资中额外给你 150 英镑，或者类似的情况。

sentences.en: They'll compensate you for that.
sentences.zh: 他们会为此补偿你。

sentences.en: But a lot of them won't.
sentences.zh: 但很多公司不会。

sentences.en: They'll just say, well, okay, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 他们只会说，好吧，没问题。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: But the sooner you start, the bigger those numbers are, much further down the line.
sentences.zh: 但你开始得越早，这些数字在未来就会越大。

sentences.en: And it also fundamentally means that when you get to your 40s and 50s, you're not having to play catch up to make up for those early years.
sentences.zh: 这也从根本上意味着，当你到了 40 多岁和 50 多岁时，你不必为了弥补早年的损失而拼命追赶。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's two things I want to talk to you about which aren't linked to pensions, but I'm going to ask you anyway because it's made me think.
sentences.zh: 有两件事我想和你谈谈，它们与养老金无关，但我还是想问你，因为这让我有所思考。

sentences.en: Okay, go on.
sentences.zh: 好的，请说。

sentences.en: About a month ago, we were talking about compound interest because I'd shared a post on socials that said,
sentences.zh: 大约一个月前，我们谈到了复利，因为我在社交媒体上分享了一篇文章，上面写着：

sentences.en: If I was to give you one penny a day that will double every day for the next 31 days, or I was to give you a million pounds today, which would you take?
sentences.zh: 如果我每天给你一便士，并且在接下来的 31 天里每天翻倍，或者我今天给你一百万英镑，你会选哪一个？

sentences.en: And most of us, I think, you wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大多数人，你不会选前者。

sentences.en: I know what you'd take.
sentences.zh: 我知道你会选什么。

sentences.en: The answer was like, of course I'd take a million pounds because one P a day doubled for 31 days.
sentences.zh: 答案就像是，我当然会选一百万英镑，因为每天一便士翻倍 31 天，

sentences.en: That's what's going to give me about four pounds or something, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那只会给我大约四英镑左右，不是吗？

sentences.en: That'd be rubbish.
sentences.zh: 那太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But actually, you're much better off with the one P a day.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，每天一便士的选择要好得多。

sentences.en: And that, in essence, is how compound interest works, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 本质上，这就是复利的工作原理，不是吗？

sentences.en: Can you guide us through that better than I just have, Ian?
sentences.zh: Ian，你能比我刚才讲得更好吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对可以。

sentences.en: So it's a great way to just illustrate a simple compact.
sentences.zh: 这是一个说明简单概念的好方法。

sentences.en: And the phrase that I always use is Einstein said it was the eighth wonder of the world.
sentences.zh: 我经常引用的一句话是，爱因斯坦曾说它是世界第八大奇迹。

sentences.en: So compound growth is just growth on your growth.
sentences.zh: 所以复利增长就是增长之上的增长。

sentences.en: So day one, you put 100 pounds in.
sentences.zh: 第一天，你投入 100 英镑。

sentences.en: So let's assume day two, you've got £102.
sentences.zh: 假设第二天，你有 102 英镑。

sentences.en: On day three, you would get growth on that 100 plus the two.
sentences.zh: 第三天，你将在 100 英镑加上那 2 英镑的基础上获得增长。

sentences.en: So it's growth on growth on growth.
sentences.zh: 所以它是增长之上的增长，再叠加增长。

sentences.en: And I think the interesting part is the longer you have that money in there, the bigger that growth is going to be,
sentences.zh: 我认为有趣的部分是，你持有这笔钱的时间越长，增长就会越大，

sentences.en: which is where, certainly when you look at pensions and investments for clients, it's a case of thinking, well, you might not be there now, but stick with it
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，当你为客户查看养老金和投资时，你会想，好吧，你现在可能还没达到那个阶段，但要坚持下去，

sentences.en: because those last few years before you need that, that compound growth can be phenomenal.
sentences.zh: 因为在需要用钱之前的最后几年，复利增长可能是惊人的。

sentences.en: But going back to your example, it's just sit down, sit down, write it on a sheet of paper.
sentences.zh: 但回到你的例子，只要坐下来，拿出一张纸写下来。

sentences.en: So a penny, then it goes to two, then it goes to four, then it'll go to eight, then it'll go to...
sentences.zh: 一便士，然后变成两便士，然后变成四便士，然后变成八便士，然后变成……

sentences.en: And it just grows and grows and grows up for a period of time.
sentences.zh: 它就这样在一段时间内不断增长。

sentences.en: And even I was amazed when I kind of looked at that one.
sentences.zh: 即使是我在看到那个结果时也感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I thought, wow, that's a big number at the end of it.
sentences.zh: 我想，哇，最后那个数字太大了。

sentences.en: But that's the kind of stuff that can either work with you or can work against you.
sentences.zh: 但这就是那种既能为你所用，也可能对你不利的东西。

sentences.en: And when I say work against you, that is things like debt, credit card loans, compound growth is working against you.
sentences.zh: 当我说是对你不利时，是指债务、信用卡贷款，复利增长正在对你不利。

sentences.en: But if you put it working for you in savings accounts, even at the moment, because the interest rates are really good or investments, you're getting growth on your growth.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把它投入到储蓄账户中，即使是现在，因为利率非常好，或者进行投资，你就能获得增长之上的增长。

sentences.en: So your money is working hard for you.
sentences.zh: 所以你的钱在为你努力工作。

sentences.en: And a phrase that I always use is, when you save your money, you put it to reSt.
sentences.zh: 我经常用的一句话是，当你存钱时，你让钱休息了。

sentences.en: When you invest your money, you put it out to work.
sentences.zh: 当你投资时，你让钱去工作了。

sentences.en: So you're sending it out of the pack, lunch, ready to go.
sentences.zh: 所以你把它派出去，带着午餐，准备出发。

sentences.en: And you're building money on your money.
sentences.zh: 你在用钱生钱。

sentences.en: And over a period of time, it makes such a difference.
sentences.zh: 经过一段时间，这会产生巨大的差异。

sentences.en: I absolutely love that.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这个说法。

sentences.en: Go on, money, off you go.
sentences.zh: 去吧，钱，出发吧。

sentences.en: Go and work hard and bring me some more back.
sentences.zh: 去努力工作，给我带回更多钱来。

sentences.en: The other thing I wanted to talk to you about is probably something that's already on your radar.
sentences.zh: 我想和你谈的另一件事可能已经在你的关注范围内了。

sentences.en: It's something I heard on Radio 2 recently.
sentences.zh: 这是我最近在 Radio 2 上听到的。

sentences.en: I'm a Radio 2 girl.
sentences.zh: 我是个听BBC Radio 2的人。

sentences.en: And they were talking about, you know, when you're in a supermarket and it says, or even for that matter, McDonald's, and they say,
sentences.zh: 他们当时在讨论，你知道，当你去超市，甚至是麦当劳的时候，他们会说，

sentences.en: oh, do you want to round it up to give to charity?
sentences.zh: 哦，你想凑个整捐给慈善机构吗？

sentences.en: You know, give an extra 25p.
sentences.zh: 你知道，多捐个25便士。

sentences.en: And I've always thought, oh, that's a nice thing for them to do, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得，哦，这对他们来说是件好事，不是吗？

sentences.en: And sometimes I do and sometimes I don't.
sentences.zh: 有时候我会捐，有时候不会。

sentences.en: What I didn't realise, and I might have grasped the conversation wrong, is that that becomes a tax break for the company.
sentences.zh: 但我没意识到的是——也许是我误解了那段对话——这其实成了公司的减税优惠。

sentences.en: That's not necessarily as altruistic as that might look.
sentences.zh: 这看起来并不一定像表面上那么无私。

sentences.en: And that's something that I wasn't aware of.
sentences.zh: 这是我之前不知道的事情。

sentences.en: And I would probably assume most people are not.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人可能都不知道。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: A hundred percent it is.
sentences.zh: 百分之百是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So they get a deduction for any charitable contributions against their corporation tax bill.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以把任何慈善捐款从企业所得税账单中扣除。

sentences.en: They don't get above and beyond that.
sentences.zh: 他们得到的优惠仅限于此，不会更多。

sentences.en: So if you said, I'm going to give you 25p in my pound to go towards the McDonald's charities, then they just get a tax break on that part that goes in.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你说，我愿意从我的一英镑里拿出25便士捐给麦当劳的慈善项目，那么他们只能就这部分捐款获得减税。

sentences.en: They don't get extra relief on top of it for doing it.
sentences.zh: 他们不会因为做了这件事而获得额外的税收减免。

sentences.en: But yeah, that's what it's there for.
sentences.zh: 但确实，这就是它的存在意义。

sentences.en: But I can remember, I used to work at McDonald's a long, long time ago.
sentences.zh: 但我记得，我很久很久以前在麦当劳工作过。

sentences.en: And at the time, they were one of the biggest charities in the world because of the amount of money that they donate to kids' charities.
sentences.zh: 当时，因为他们向儿童慈善机构捐赠的金额巨大，他们是世界上规模最大的慈善机构之一。

sentences.en: I think they do a phenomenal job.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们做得非常出色。

sentences.en: But at the same time, that's something that you could benefit from.
sentences.zh: 但同时，这也是你可以从中受益的事情。

sentences.en: Like if there are charities that are close to your heart, rather than contributing to them personally, you could contribute to them through your business.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你有心仪的慈善机构，与其个人捐款，不如通过你的企业进行捐赠。

sentences.en: And you could legitimately write some of that off as a taxable expense.
sentences.zh: 你可以合法地将其中一部分作为应纳税支出进行抵扣。

sentences.en: Like make the most of it, you know, contribute out of your business.
sentences.zh: 尽量利用这一点，你知道，从你的企业里进行捐赠。

sentences.en: So if people are already limited companies, then they can look to do that in their own business and then benefit the charities that they want to benefit.
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们已经有了有限公司，他们可以考虑在自己的企业里这样做，从而惠及他们想要支持的慈善机构。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对可以。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: How many stars did you get on your badge, Ian?
sentences.zh: Ian，你的徽章上有几颗星？

sentences.en: Oh, great question.
sentences.zh: 哦，问得好。

sentences.en: I had, this is the old school.
sentences.zh: 我有，这是老派的做法。

sentences.en: I had the full house.
sentences.zh: 我拿到了满贯。

sentences.en: I had five.
sentences.zh: 我有五颗星。

sentences.en: So I did a bit of everything.
sentences.zh: 所以我什么都干过一点。

sentences.en: Honestly, I talked to people at McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我跟麦当劳的人聊过。

sentences.en: It was a great, I loved McDonald's when I worked there.
sentences.zh: 那是一段很棒的经历，我在麦当劳工作时很喜欢那里。

sentences.en: It was a really busy branch and it just, they got the monies with that out of you, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 那是一家非常繁忙的分店，他们确实能把你的潜能榨干，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: But I loved it.
sentences.zh: 但我很喜欢。

sentences.en: I think it was such a great grounding to do so many things that I kind of look at now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一个很好的基础，让我现在回头看，能做很多事情。

sentences.en: Because you were just in at the deep end and you worked really, really hard for eight hour shifts.
sentences.zh: 因为你直接被扔进深水区，而且八小时轮班工作非常非常辛苦。

sentences.en: Stunk of burgers at the end of it, which me parents never liked, but there you go.
sentences.zh: 下班时浑身一股汉堡味，我父母从来不喜欢这样，但没办法。

sentences.en: One of my besties when I was at uni used to work at McDonald's during the school holidays as well.
sentences.zh: 我在大学时最好的朋友之一，在学校假期时也曾在麦当劳工作过。

sentences.en: And we used to like to play a game.
sentences.zh: 我们当时喜欢玩一个游戏。

sentences.en: How bored we were sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我们当时有多无聊啊。

sentences.en: What do McDonald's ever run out of?
sentences.zh: 麦当劳有什么是会卖光的吗？

sentences.en: Do they ever run out of gherkins?
sentences.zh: 他们会用完酸黄瓜吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: Do they ever run out of buns?
sentences.zh: 他们会用完面包吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: And literally the answer was no for everything.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上，所有东西的答案都是不会。

sentences.en: But I think things have changed these days.
sentences.zh: 但我认为现在情况变了。

sentences.en: They often don't have things these days.
sentences.zh: 如今他们经常缺货。

sentences.en: But yeah, that's a little insight into my life when I was at uni.
sentences.zh: 但这就是我大学生活的一点小插曲。

sentences.en: Also, they're a really good employer.
sentences.zh: 另外，他们是一个非常好的雇主。

sentences.en: They do private health care for their staff, which you just wouldn't know probably.
sentences.zh: 他们为员工提供私人医疗保险，你可能根本不知道。

sentences.en: And degree.
sentences.zh: 还有学位。

sentences.en: You can get a degree now through McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以通过麦当劳获得学位。

sentences.en: I've read a great book.
sentences.zh: 我读过一本很棒的书。

sentences.en: It was called Simple, Logical, Repeatable, which is one of the former directors of McDonald's in the US.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《简单、逻辑、可重复》，作者是麦当劳美国的前任董事之一。

sentences.en: And she wrote a book around how processes will help define your business.
sentences.zh: 她写了一本书，讲述流程如何帮助定义你的业务。

sentences.en: And it's so true because McDonald's are really, really good at what they do because you get the same cheeseburger no matter where in the world you get it because it's a simple,
sentences.zh: 这太真实了，因为麦当劳在他们的领域做得非常非常出色，无论你在世界哪个角落买到的芝士汉堡都是一样的，因为这是一个简单、

sentences.en: logical, repeatable process.
sentences.zh: 逻辑性强、可重复的流程。

sentences.en: And they've just refined and refined and refined that down to something and distilled it to something really pure.
sentences.zh: 他们不断地提炼、提炼、再提炼，将其精简到非常纯粹的地步。

sentences.en: And every single branch follows the same process.
sentences.zh: 每一家分店都遵循同样的流程。

sentences.en: Every employee goes through the same process.
sentences.zh: 每一位员工都经历同样的流程。

sentences.en: Their training is exceptional because they want everybody to do it in a specific way.
sentences.zh: 他们的培训非常出色，因为他们希望每个人都以特定的方式去做。

sentences.en: They've done phenomenally well out of it.
sentences.zh: 他们从中获得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: I don't know whether you've seen the film with Michael Keaton in it when he's the Ray Kroc, the founder of McDonald's, and he gets involved in these two.
sentences.zh: 不知道你有没有看过迈克尔·基顿主演的那部电影，他饰演麦当劳创始人雷·克洛克，他卷入了那两兄弟的事情中。

sentences.en: Brilliant film.
sentences.zh: 很棒的电影。

sentences.en: Love that film.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢那部电影。

sentences.en: But, yeah, there's so much to be learned from it.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，从中可以学到很多东西。

sentences.en: They've done phenomenally well.
sentences.zh: 他们做得非常成功。

sentences.en: They're a worldwide chain and continue to grow.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个全球连锁企业，并且还在持续增长。

sentences.en: So, one of the questions I've received was given the kind of uncertainty of what a career in mental health might look like these days.
sentences.zh: 所以，我收到的一个问题是，考虑到如今心理健康职业前景的不确定性。

sentences.en: So, it might involve, you know, NHS or employed work.
sentences.zh: 它可能涉及，你知道，NHS（英国国家医疗服务体系）或受雇工作。

sentences.en: It might involve a bit of private work.
sentences.zh: 它可能涉及一些私人工作。

sentences.en: It might involve fully being private.
sentences.zh: 它可能涉及完全从事私人执业。

sentences.en: Should people or could people consider, should they not have any NHS pension?
sentences.zh: 人们是否应该或可以考虑，如果他们没有任何NHS养老金的话？

sentences.en: Should they start a private pension right away?
sentences.zh: 他们应该立即开始存私人养老金吗？

sentences.en: Or, I know it's kind of hard to give generic advice, but people are confused, Ian.
sentences.zh: 或者，我知道很难给出通用的建议，但人们感到困惑，Ian。

sentences.en: What's the way forward?
sentences.zh: 未来的路该怎么走？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that's in the whole of the market about pensions.
sentences.zh: 我认为整个养老金市场都存在这个问题。

sentences.en: Like, pensions have this illusion that they're really complicated.
sentences.zh: 养老金给人一种非常复杂的错觉。

sentences.en: But if you look at the NHS pension, it's still a very, very good pension scheme.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看NHS养老金，它仍然是一个非常、非常好的养老金计划。

sentences.en: So, I would encourage anybody that has access to their pension scheme to have one because it's such a well-rounded, great growth on the scheme itself,
sentences.zh: 所以我鼓励任何有权加入该养老金计划的人都去加入，因为它非常全面，计划本身的增长非常棒，

sentences.en: dependent on which variation of the scheme that you're involved in.
sentences.zh: 取决于你参与的是哪种变体计划。

sentences.en: But even the most recent one, which I think was the 2015 edition, I can't remember off the top of my head.
sentences.zh: 但即使是最近的一个版本，我想是2015版的，我记不太清了。

sentences.en: But there's three different evolutions of the NHS pension, and no matter which evolution you're involved in, you're not going to get that kind of growth.
sentences.zh: NHS养老金有三种不同的演变版本，无论你参与的是哪一种，你都无法获得那种增长。

sentences.en: You're not going to get that kind of return over a consistent basis as you would do with a private pension.
sentences.zh: 你无法像私人养老金那样获得持续的基础回报。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean to say that a private pension hasn't got its place.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着私人养老金没有它的用武之地。

sentences.en: So, ultimately, if you are thinking that you want to move from the NHS to private practice, there are pros and cons for both of them.
sentences.zh: 所以，归根结底，如果你正在考虑从NHS转向私人执业，两者各有利弊。

sentences.en: What I encourage psychologists and people that work in this space that I have conversations with is to think about the bigger picture, first of all.
sentences.zh: 我鼓励心理学家和在这个领域工作、与我交流的人，首先要考虑大局。

sentences.en: It's not just about the pension.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是养老金的问题。

sentences.en: It's about the big piece.
sentences.zh: 这是关于大局的问题。

sentences.en: It's what do you want to get out of life?
sentences.zh: 你从生活中想要得到什么？

sentences.en: What are your financial goals?
sentences.zh: 你的财务目标是什么？

sentences.en: What do you want to achieve?
sentences.zh: 你想要实现什么？

sentences.en: Why is that so important to you?
sentences.zh: 为什么这对你如此重要？

sentences.en: And plan that all out and get a real structure that works, that you're emotionally engaged with first, and then the numbers can just drop in.
sentences.zh: 把这些都规划好，建立一个真正有效的结构，让你首先在情感上投入其中，然后数字自然就会填补进去。

sentences.en: Because it might be that you've got enough pension provision where you are after being in the NHS for 10 or 15 years that you don't necessarily want to have a private pension.
sentences.zh: 因为可能你在NHS工作了10到15年后，已经有了足够的养老金保障，你未必非要一份私人养老金。

sentences.en: There might be other things you want to do.
sentences.zh: 可能还有其他你想做的事情。

sentences.en: It might be that you've got a shortfall, so you want to make that up by making those contributions and keeping your corporation tax below a certain level.
sentences.zh: 也可能你存在缺口，所以你想通过增加缴费并将企业所得税保持在一定水平以下来弥补。

sentences.en: Everybody's different.
sentences.zh: 每个人都不同。

sentences.en: And what I'd encourage anybody to do is have some conversations with a financial advisor, have some conversations with an accountant, talk these things through, talk to colleagues,
sentences.zh: 我鼓励任何人做的是，与财务顾问谈谈，与会计师谈谈，把这些事情讨论清楚，与同事交流，

sentences.en: talk to other people in this position to understand what they do.
sentences.zh: 与处于同样位置的其他人交流，了解他们是怎么做的。

sentences.en: I think the NHS have got a great help plan that you can get in contact with with a pension.
sentences.zh: 我认为NHS有一个很棒的帮助计划，你可以联系他们咨询养老金。

sentences.en: The information might be limited, but it's a good starting point.
sentences.zh: 信息可能有限，但这是一个很好的起点。

sentences.en: Most financial advisors will have a conversation with you around what's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 大多数财务顾问都会和你讨论什么是正确的做法。

sentences.en: And I'd like to think the majority of them would be would would indeed come back with that right advice for you.
sentences.zh: 而且我愿意相信，他们中的大多数人确实会为你提供正确的建议。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: And you can absolutely have both, can't you?
sentences.zh: 而且你完全可以两者兼得，不是吗？

sentences.en: You can have an NHS and a private and also a child can have a pension.
sentences.zh: 你可以同时拥有NHS养老金和私人养老金，而且孩子也可以有养老金。

sentences.en: You can start saving a pension for a child, can't you?
sentences.zh: 你可以开始为孩子存养老金，对吧？

sentences.en: Literally, it's never too soon.
sentences.zh: 真的，永远都不嫌早。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think if you can start contributing to a pension for your kids at an early age, you're setting themselves up for such a great retirement further down the line.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为如果你能尽早开始为孩子缴纳养老金，你就是在为他们未来的退休生活打下非常好的基础。

sentences.en: And as I said earlier, starting earlier makes such a difference.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，早点开始会有很大的不同。

sentences.en: If you could get them started from what they wouldn't start from birth, like parents or grandparents contributed from birth.
sentences.zh: 如果你能让他们从出生就开始，比如父母或祖父母从出生起就开始缴费。

sentences.en: You could do 2,880 a year with tax relief that goes up to 3,600.
sentences.zh: 你可以每年存2880英镑，加上税收减免，总额可达3600英镑。

sentences.en: If you contributed to that and they then contributed a hundred pound a month for the rest of their life.
sentences.zh: 如果你存了这笔钱，然后他们余生每月再存一百英镑。

sentences.en: They're the kind of people that retire at the age of 55 and the rest of us are kind of kind of working.
sentences.zh: 他们就是那种55岁就能退休的人，而我们其他人还在忙着工作。

sentences.en: And it makes such a difference,
sentences.zh: 这真的有很大的不同，

sentences.en: but having that discipline of a hundred pound a month rather than getting to 40 and 50 and realizing you've got some serious shortfalls to make up makes such a difference.
sentences.zh: 但拥有每月存一百英镑的纪律，总比到了40岁、50岁才意识到自己有严重的缺口需要弥补要好得多。

sentences.en: And if people are listening and thinking, oh, I'd love to be able to find an extra hundred pounds a month to put in my kid's pension, but I haven't got that,
sentences.zh: 如果有人在听，心想，哦，我很想每月多存一百英镑到孩子的养老金里，但我没有那么多钱，

sentences.en: but I could probably muster up a tenner a month.
sentences.zh: 但我可能每月能凑出十英镑。

sentences.en: Is that worth doing or not?
sentences.zh: 这样做值得吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, whatever you can do.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽你所能就好。

sentences.en: I think investments and pensions are a lot more accessible than they ever have been.
sentences.zh: 我认为投资和养老金比以往任何时候都更容易接触到。

sentences.en: I think the information that's available, especially with social media and webinars, YouTube, places like that, there is a vast amount of information available on the basics.
sentences.zh: 我认为现有的信息，特别是通过社交媒体、网络研讨会、YouTube之类的地方，关于基础知识的信息量非常巨大。

sentences.en: And I think you almost need to distill it down to what the basic elements are.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你几乎需要将其提炼出基本要素。

sentences.en: And it's, do you want to save for your kid's future?
sentences.zh: 那就是，你想为孩子的未来储蓄吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to save for your future?
sentences.zh: 你想为自己的未来储蓄吗？

sentences.en: Yes or no?
sentences.zh: 是还是不是？

sentences.en: Simple as that.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: And then you can kind of plan out.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以开始规划了。

sentences.en: You don't necessarily have to start with a massive amount.
sentences.zh: 你不一定非要从一大笔钱开始。

sentences.en: It could be that you start, like you said, with a tenner, that maybe you build up in a savings account and then once a year, you make a contribution into the pension.
sentences.zh: 你可以像你说的，从十英镑开始，也许先存进储蓄账户，然后一年一次，再存入养老金账户。

sentences.en: I'm not sure many investment platforms operate at only a tenner a month.
sentences.zh: 我不确定有多少投资平台支持每月仅十英镑的额度。

sentences.en: I think the minimum tends to be about 25, but two and a half months in, you can make that contribution.
sentences.zh: 我想最低限额通常在25英镑左右，但两个半月存一次，你就可以进行那笔缴费。

sentences.en: You could do that three, four, five times a year if you wanted to, but just get started and start chipping away.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，一年可以存三、四、五次，只要开始行动，一点点积累起来。

sentences.en: It makes a big difference.
sentences.zh: 这会有很大的不同。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Such good advice.
sentences.zh: 非常好的建议。

sentences.en: And when I left the NHS, you know, it's that quandary of, what do I do with it?
sentences.zh: 当我离开NHS时，你知道，面临着一个困境，我该怎么处理它？

sentences.en: Do I leave it there?
sentences.zh: 我把它留在那里吗？

sentences.en: Do I kind of take it out and put it in my new, shiny private pension?
sentences.zh: 我是把它取出来，放进我新的、闪亮的私人养老金里吗？

sentences.en: And I think the general consensus is leave it there.
sentences.zh: 我认为普遍的共识是留在那里。

sentences.en: Leave it there.
sentences.zh: 留在那里。

sentences.en: You're not going to do much better than an NHS pension.
sentences.zh: 你不会找到比NHS养老金更好的选择了。

sentences.en: Is that kind of your general advice?
sentences.zh: 这算是你的一般性建议吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, 100%.
sentences.zh: 是的，百分之百。

sentences.en: I mean, you can't move it out anyway, so it has to stay within the NHS.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，反正你也没法把它转出来，所以它必须留在国民医疗服务体系（NHS）内。

sentences.en: I think one of the dangers that you can kind of overlook is you can almost kind of disregard that and start really going aggressively after your private pension and contributing consistently on a consistent basis over a period of time.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种危险容易被忽视，那就是你几乎可以忽略这一点，开始真正积极地投入私人养老金，并在一段时间内持续地进行供款。

sentences.en: Take a step back, big picture stuff that has to be included in that conversation.
sentences.zh: 退一步看，在谈话中必须包含大局观的内容。

sentences.en: If you're having a conversation with a financial advisor and all they're talking about is the private pension, but they're not including this NHS pension that you've got,
sentences.zh: 如果你正在和理财顾问交谈，而他们只谈论私人养老金，却不把你拥有的这份NHS养老金考虑在内，

sentences.en: which could be worth quite a tidy sum of money, then maybe you need to be having conversations with a different financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 而这份养老金可能价值不菲，那么也许你需要换一位理财顾问谈谈了。

sentences.en: And that's not me saying that it has to be me or anybody else, but big picture stuff, you need to plan the whole thing out.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说一定要找我或者其他人，但从大局出发，你需要对整体进行规划。

sentences.en: It's not just looking at one particular area.
sentences.zh: 不能只盯着某一个特定领域。

sentences.en: And yes, those private contributions are worth it long term, but how do you know you haven't got enough already?
sentences.zh: 没错，长期来看私人供款是值得的，但你怎么知道你现在的钱还不够呢？

sentences.en: Because if you have got enough already, could you do something else?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你已经足够了，你是不是可以做点别的？

sentences.en: Could you be spending it?
sentences.zh: 是不是可以把它花掉？

sentences.en: Could you be going on holiday two or three times a year instead of paying into that pension?
sentences.zh: 是不是可以每年去度假两三次，而不是把钱存进养老金里？

sentences.en: That's why the big picture conversation makes such a difference.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么从大局出发的谈话会产生如此大的差异。

sentences.en: Retirement plan is really important, 100%, but it's that million dollar question of getting a balance between now and what you want further down the line.
sentences.zh: 退休计划确实非常重要，百分之百重要，但如何在当下和你未来想要的生活之间取得平衡，这是一个价值百万美元的问题。

sentences.en: And somewhere in the middle is the right answer.
sentences.zh: 而答案就在中间的某个位置。

sentences.en: And that balance will tip and kind of sway throughout your life.
sentences.zh: 这种平衡会随着你的人生不断倾斜和摇摆。

sentences.en: And sometimes I tell clients to just spend the money and it kind of puts them on a bit of the back foot.
sentences.zh: 有时我会告诉客户直接把钱花掉，这让他们有点措手不及。

sentences.en: But if you've got enough, then why do you need more?
sentences.zh: 但如果你已经足够了，为什么还需要更多呢？

sentences.en: Spend it, enjoy life, because tomorrow is not guaranteed, is it?
sentences.zh: 花掉它，享受生活，因为明天是无法保证的，不是吗？

sentences.en: No, it isn't.
sentences.zh: 不，确实无法保证。

sentences.en: And I've not read the book, but I know there's a book called, is it Die Broke or something like that?
sentences.zh: 我没读过那本书，但我知道有一本书叫什么《死时破产》（Die Broke）之类的？

sentences.en: That you basically plan so much that you're, you know, you haven't really got anything left to pass on when you're gone.
sentences.zh: 就是说你基本上把一切都规划好了，以至于当你离开时，真的没剩下什么留给别人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I've heard it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我听说过。

sentences.en: I can't remember the exact name of it.
sentences.zh: 我不记得确切的名字了。

sentences.en: I don't think it's something along those lines.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不是那个名字，但大概是那个意思。

sentences.en: Yes, it's definitely on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，它绝对在书单上。

sentences.en: But yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但确实如此。

sentences.en: Like, you can't take it with you.
sentences.zh: 就像那句话说的，你带不走这些钱。

sentences.en: I mean, great that you want to leave stuff for the kids.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你想给孩子们留点东西是好事。

sentences.en: I understand that as well, because actually it's given them a bit of a leg up further down the line.
sentences.zh: 我也理解这一点，因为这确实能让他们在未来过得轻松一点。

sentences.en: But I'm sure your kids, and I'd say this exactly for my parents, I'd prefer them to be around for another 10 or 15 years, because I've had a great old life.
sentences.zh: 但我相信你的孩子们——我对我父母也是这么说的——我更希望他们能再多活个10到15年，因为我已经过得很好了。

sentences.en: Rather than scrimping, saving and leave me 50, 60 grand in a will, spend it.
sentences.zh: 与其省吃俭用在遗嘱里给我留下五六万英镑，不如把钱花掉。

sentences.en: I don't need it.
sentences.zh: 我不需要那些钱。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I wish I could have kept my dad for longer.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我能让父亲多陪我一段时间。

sentences.en: You know, he worked hard and he worked as a boiler man.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他工作很努力，是一名锅炉工。

sentences.en: And, you know, he did enjoy his life.
sentences.zh: 而且，他确实享受了他的生活。

sentences.en: He liked tinkering with his bikes and stuff, but he died at 71 and that's no age.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢摆弄他的自行车之类的东西，但他71岁就去世了，那根本不算老。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不算。

sentences.en: And they just saved, you know, they didn't really have new cars and didn't have fancy holidays.
sentences.zh: 他们只是省钱，你知道，他们真的没买过新车，也没去过什么豪华度假。

sentences.en: And it's just, yeah, it always feels like a distant thing, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这感觉总是很遥远，对吧？

sentences.en: All this financial planning and when we're going to retire.
sentences.zh: 所有这些财务规划和我们何时退休的问题。

sentences.en: And, but I was recently staying with somebody in Ireland when I was over there doing a keynote talk and the lady I was staying with was 80, 84 and I'm 42.
sentences.zh: 但我最近在爱尔兰做主题演讲时住在一个人家里，那位女士84岁，而我42岁。

sentences.en: And I literally had this moment of just thinking, gosh, that's nothing.
sentences.zh: 我当时真的产生了一种想法，天哪，那根本不算什么。

sentences.en: You're exactly double my age.
sentences.zh: 你正好是我的两倍大。

sentences.en: And it feels like that's no time at all.
sentences.zh: 感觉那根本不需要多少时间。

sentences.en: Before I know it, I will be 84.
sentences.zh: 在我意识到之前，我就已经84岁了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Disappear so quick.
sentences.zh: 时间过得太快了。

sentences.en: And I see that so often and you can, as much as you're trying, I talk to clients about this,
sentences.zh: 我经常看到这种情况，无论你多么努力，我和客户谈论这个时，

sentences.en: having a North Star in the sky of where you want to get to and where you want to plan and move towards.
sentences.zh: 就像在天空中设定一颗北极星，指引你想去的地方，以及你想规划和前进的方向。

sentences.en: That doesn't have to be rigid.
sentences.zh: 那不必是僵化的。

sentences.en: That can move.
sentences.zh: 它可以移动。

sentences.en: That can change.
sentences.zh: 它可以改变。

sentences.en: And it will because I've seen it and know that most people have seen it over a period of time.
sentences.zh: 而且它一定会改变，因为我见过，而且我知道大多数人在一段时间内都见过这种情况。

sentences.en: You make all these best laid plans and then something just throws a spanner in the works and it has to change.
sentences.zh: 你做好了所有最周密的计划，然后突然出了岔子，一切都必须改变。

sentences.en: Maybe your partner gets ill.
sentences.zh: 也许你的伴侣生病了。

sentences.en: Maybe you split up.
sentences.zh: 也许你们分开了。

sentences.en: Maybe you get divorced.
sentences.zh: 也许你们离婚了。

sentences.en: There's lots of different moving parts in this.
sentences.zh: 这里面有很多不同的变数。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean you disregard it completely and live completely for the now.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着你要完全无视它，只顾活在当下。

sentences.en: It's a hard act and a hard balance to get right because society at the moment and how we live is expensive.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难把握的平衡，因为目前的社会和我们的生活方式成本很高。

sentences.en: We're in the middle of a cost of living crisis.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于生活成本危机的中心。

sentences.en: We've got high interest rates.
sentences.zh: 我们面临着高利率。

sentences.en: So if your mortgage is changing, you're probably coming from 2% interest rates to 5% or 6% interest rates.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你的抵押贷款利率在变，你可能正从2%的利率变成5%或6%。

sentences.en: That has a big impact on your monthly bills.
sentences.zh: 这对你的每月账单有很大影响。

sentences.en: We all know how much more expensive supermarket shopping is, how much more expensive petrol is, how much more expensive your car insurance is.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道超市购物贵了多少，汽油贵了多少，汽车保险贵了多少。

sentences.en: Everything is getting more and more expensive.
sentences.zh: 一切都变得越来越贵。

sentences.en: That's the impact of inflation.
sentences.zh: 这就是通货膨胀的影响。

sentences.en: And when inflation is running at the rate that it is at the moment, which feels a little bit out of control,
sentences.zh: 当通货膨胀以目前的速度运行时，感觉有点失控，

sentences.en: that has a real impact on the amount that you take home every month.
sentences.zh: 这对你每月的到手收入有真正的影响。

sentences.en: And sometimes you have to just pull it all in and think, I can't think about the long term right now.
sentences.zh: 有时你不得不收缩一切，心想，我现在没法考虑长期了。

sentences.en: I've planned for that like four or five years ago, but I can't think about that right now.
sentences.zh: 我在四五年前就为那件事做过计划，但我现在没法考虑它。

sentences.en: I just need to go into survival mode.
sentences.zh: 我只需要进入生存模式。

sentences.en: And I think there's nothing wrong with that because we feel this emotional guilt that we're not going to have the life that we want further down the line.
sentences.zh: 我认为这没什么错，因为我们有一种情感上的愧疚感，觉得未来无法过上我们想要的生活。

sentences.en: Or maybe we're not going to have the round the world trip.
sentences.zh: 或者也许我们无法进行那次环球旅行。

sentences.en: But that's no good if you're miserable right now.
sentences.zh: 但如果你现在过得很痛苦，那也没什么用。

sentences.en: If you can't afford to live right now and it has an impact on you, your mental health, your well-being, your family and all the rest of it, what's the cost?
sentences.zh: 如果你现在连生活都负担不起，这对你、你的心理健康、你的幸福感、你的家庭等等都有影响，那代价是什么？

sentences.en: And you can't put pounds and pence cost on that stuff.
sentences.zh: 你无法用金钱来衡量这些东西的代价。

sentences.en: Yes, plan for the future, but it's getting that balance right.
sentences.zh: 是的，要为未来做计划，但关键在于取得平衡。

sentences.en: And that's hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: And it's hard to do it yourself when you've got emotion involved in it.
sentences.zh: 当你身处其中带有个人情感时，很难自己做到这一点。

sentences.en: Because sometimes somebody else has an extra pair of eyes and ears, can see things and have the same conversation you've been having yourself.
sentences.zh: 因为有时别人能提供额外的视角，能看到一些东西，并进行和你自己内心一样的对话。

sentences.en: But it sounds differently and it just resonates on a different level to having that conversation with yourself.
sentences.zh: 但听起来感觉不同，它在另一个层面上引起了共鸣，而不是仅仅和你自己对话。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's really, really useful food for thought.
sentences.zh: 这真的是非常有用的思考素材。

sentences.en: Am I right in thinking that if the worst happens and we don't get to that ripe old age that we'd planned for our retirement,
sentences.zh: 我想得对吗？如果最坏的情况发生了，我们没能活到我们为退休计划的那个高龄，

sentences.en: that certainly a private pension can be passed on as an asset.
sentences.zh: 那么私人养老金肯定可以作为资产传承下去。

sentences.en: So that then becomes something that you leave for your children.
sentences.zh: 所以它就成了你留给孩子的东西。

sentences.en: Am I right in that?
sentences.zh: 我这样理解对吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对正确。

sentences.en: So, I mean, NHS pension, you can do the same thing, but the benefits are slightly less.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，NHS养老金也可以这样做，但福利稍微少一些。

sentences.en: So, the NHS pension, we'll start with that one.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们先从NHS养老金说起。

sentences.en: So, that's a defined benefit scheme.
sentences.zh: 那是一个固定收益计划。

sentences.en: So, with a degree of predictability, you've got an idea of how much income you're going to have from that pension scheme when you retire.
sentences.zh: 所以，在一定程度的可预测性下，你对退休后能从该养老金计划中获得多少收入是有概念的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, as much as they're great for you and the income that you're going to have with your spouse or your partner, whoever else it might be, if something happens to you,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管它们对你和你配偶或伴侣（无论其他人是谁）未来能获得的收入很有保障，但如果你发生了什么事，

sentences.en: those benefits reduce significantly.
sentences.zh: 这些福利会显著减少。

sentences.en: So, typically, it would be reduced down to, say, 50%.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，它会减少到，比如说，50%。

sentences.en: So, if you've got an income of, say, $30,000 from your pension, then it would reduce down to $15,000.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你从养老金中获得3万英镑的收入，那么它会减少到1.5万英镑。

sentences.en: So, your spouse would get $15,000.
sentences.zh: 所以你的配偶会得到1.5万英镑。

sentences.en: If your spouse then passes away, nothing then gets left to the kids.
sentences.zh: 如果你的配偶随后去世，那么就不会留下任何东西给孩子们了。

sentences.en: Unless they're under the age of 21 in full-time education, where they would get, I think it's a 25% pension,
sentences.zh: 除非他们未满21岁且在接受全日制教育，那样他们会得到，我想是25%的养老金，

sentences.en: but that would only be while they're considered to be financially dependent upon you.
sentences.zh: 但这仅限于他们被认为在经济上依赖你的时候。

sentences.en: Flip that over to the other side, and then you've got a private pension.
sentences.zh: 转到另一边，你就有私人养老金了。

sentences.en: In simple terms, just think of it like a savings account.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，把它想象成一个储蓄账户。

sentences.en: So, it's the £100,000 pension pot.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个10万英镑的养老金池。

sentences.en: That could be passed down to your kids, your partner, whoever it is that you decide.
sentences.zh: 它可以传给你的孩子、你的伴侣，或者任何你决定的人。

sentences.en: And that's done really simply when you set the pension up with your financial advisor, or even if you haven't used a financial advisor,
sentences.zh: 当你和理财顾问设立养老金时，这很容易做到，即使你没有使用理财顾问，

sentences.en: you're completing an expression of wish form.
sentences.zh: 你也可以填写一份意愿表达表。

sentences.en: And that's you saying, I want my pension to go to little Johnny, little Jane, and me partner, Mary.
sentences.zh: 那就是你在说，我希望我的养老金留给小约翰、小简，还有我的伴侣玛丽。

sentences.en: I don't know where those names came from, but they were the first ones that popped into the head.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这些名字是从哪儿来的，但它们是脑子里蹦出来的第一个名字。

sentences.en: But they're the ones that you pass that pension down to.
sentences.zh: 但他们就是你把养老金传给的人。

sentences.en: They can do whatever you want with it.
sentences.zh: 他们可以用它做任何你想做的事。

sentences.en: Now, the tax benefits would be that if you died before the age of 75, they get that lump sum as a, they can do whatever they want with.
sentences.zh: 现在，税收优惠在于，如果你在75岁之前去世，他们可以获得那笔一次性付款，他们可以用它做任何想做的事。

sentences.en: They can keep it in a pension, or they can take it out.
sentences.zh: 他们可以把它留在养老金里，或者取出来。

sentences.en: After 75, there's some tax implications.
sentences.zh: 75岁之后，会有一些税务影响。

sentences.en: So, most of the time, people will just keep that as part of a pension.
sentences.zh: 所以，大多数时候，人们会把它作为养老金的一部分保留下来。

sentences.en: But I like to talk to clients about it and think of your pension as almost like an extra bit of life insurance.
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢和客户谈论这一点，把你的养老金看作是额外的人寿保险。

sentences.en: So, if something does happen to you, and you've got a private scheme, that could be passed down through the generations.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你真的发生了什么事，而你有一个私人计划，那就可以代代相传。

sentences.en: It doesn't necessarily have to go to your kids, because you've got your grandkids, or whoever it is.
sentences.zh: 它不一定非要给你的孩子，因为你还有孙辈，或者其他任何人。

sentences.en: Think of that as part of the bigger picture.
sentences.zh: 把这看作大局的一部分。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And you mentioned there that it's obviously possible to do investing by yourself without a financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到，显然可以在没有理财顾问的情况下自己进行投资。

sentences.en: And for some people, perhaps on a lower income, that might feel preferable.
sentences.zh: 对于一些人，也许是收入较低的人，这可能感觉更可取。

sentences.en: But I guess the theory is, is that when you go with an IFA, that they try and make you more money than you would do otherwise, if you were to do it by yourself.
sentences.zh: 但我猜理论是，当你找独立理财顾问（IFA）时，他们会试图让你比自己操作赚更多的钱。

sentences.en: It's, you know, because I guess the thing with financial advisors is that you do pay them a premium.
sentences.zh: 因为我想理财顾问的问题在于你确实要支付他们一笔费用。

sentences.en: And that can feel quite ouchy.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人觉得有点心疼。

sentences.en: And when you do have a lower income, it can feel like giving away money that just feels really hard won.
sentences.zh: 当你收入较低时，这感觉就像是在送出那些来之不易的钱。

sentences.en: How can you kind of balance up the kind of the morals and the ethics of that?
sentences.zh: 你该如何平衡其中的道德和伦理问题呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's a question and a half.
sentences.zh: 那可真是个难题。

sentences.en: I mean, you can do it yourself, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你当然可以自己做。

sentences.en: What I'd encourage you to think about is, have you got the knowledge to be able to do it yourself?
sentences.zh: 我想鼓励你思考的是，你是否有能力自己完成？

sentences.en: Because if you've got the knowledge, have you then got the time?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你有知识，你是否有时间？

sentences.en: Have you then got the capability?
sentences.zh: 你是否有执行能力？

sentences.en: And there are three different things to look at there.
sentences.zh: 这三点是需要考虑的。

sentences.en: Now, if you have, then yes, do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你都有，那么是的，去做吧。

sentences.en: If you haven't, then maybe that's the point that you engage a financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有，那么也许这就是你聘请理财顾问的时候了。

sentences.en: And there is a perception that having financial advice can be expensive.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种观念，认为获得理财建议可能很昂贵。

sentences.en: And I'd probably encourage you to think about it the other way around.
sentences.zh: 我可能会鼓励你反过来想。

sentences.en: Like, what are the costs of you not using a financial advisor?
sentences.zh: 比如，你不使用理财顾问的代价是什么？

sentences.en: Because that can be significant.
sentences.zh: 因为那可能是巨大的。

sentences.en: There are lots and lots of different studies.
sentences.zh: 有很多很多不同的研究。

sentences.en: And you can just put them into Google of financial advice versus not having financial advice.
sentences.zh: 你可以在谷歌上搜索一下“有理财建议”与“没有理财建议”的对比。

sentences.en: And I think the average difference that makes is a pension of somewhere between an extra two to three thousand pound a year when you retire.
sentences.zh: 我认为这带来的平均差异是退休后每年多出两到三千英镑的养老金。

sentences.en: Now, if you can use a financial advisor to set that up for you and have the extra two to three thousand pound a year when you retire, when you can't earn anymore,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你能利用理财顾问为你设置好，并在退休后每年多出两到三千英镑，当你无法再赚钱时，

sentences.en: that's a big difference.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的差异。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that you can't do that yourself.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着你不能自己做到这一点。

sentences.en: There are so many investment platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在有很多投资平台。

sentences.en: There are lots of self-investment platforMs.
sentences.zh: 有很多自助投资平台。

sentences.en: There are a lot of them that will have tutorials and really simple pathways that you can go down to start this thing yourself.
sentences.zh: 其中有很多平台提供教程，并为你规划了非常简单的路径，让你能够自行上手。

sentences.en: But my view is that you should be able to have a conversation with a financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 但我的观点是，你应该能够与理财顾问进行交流。

sentences.en: And certainly I do this with clients.
sentences.zh: 我当然会与客户进行这样的交流。

sentences.en: You don't need to have me as a financial advisor for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 你并不需要我终身担任你的理财顾问。

sentences.en: We can have a one-off conversation and we can do that on a basis that works for you.
sentences.zh: 我们可以进行一次性的咨询，而且可以以一种适合你的方式进行。

sentences.en: I think the whole world of financial advice is changing.
sentences.zh: 我认为整个理财咨询行业正在发生变化。

sentences.en: It's changing massively and it will do over the next 10 or 15 years.
sentences.zh: 它正在发生巨大的变革，在未来10到15年内还会持续演变。

sentences.en: The vast majority of the industry right now feels quite transactional.
sentences.zh: 目前绝大多数行业从业者给人的感觉都非常商业化。

sentences.en: So you sit down, you go through a process, listen to a guy probably in a pinstripe suit with a flash card tell you about how great their business is,
sentences.zh: 你坐下来，走一遍流程，听一个可能穿着细条纹西装、拿着闪光卡片的人告诉你他们的业务有多棒，

sentences.en: how much money they look after and why you should use them.
sentences.zh: 他们管理着多少资金，以及你为什么要选择他们。

sentences.en: And it feels a bit like a sales pitch.
sentences.zh: 这感觉有点像推销。

sentences.en: And I was part of that world for a long time until I started thinking there was a better way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 我在那个世界里待了很长时间，直到我开始思考是否有更好的方式。

sentences.en: Now, I don't operate like that anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不再那样做了。

sentences.en: My view is actually let's figure out what's really, really important to you, why that's really important to you, and then we'll fit the numbers around that.
sentences.zh: 我的观点实际上是：让我们弄清楚什么对你来说才是真正重要的，为什么它对你如此重要，然后我们再围绕这些来规划财务数据。

sentences.en: And that's not me trying to convince you for me to be your financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我在试图说服你让我做你的理财顾问。

sentences.en: It's about me planning out what's important to you.
sentences.zh: 这是关于我为你规划出对你重要的事情。

sentences.en: And if you want to go and do that yourself, because you've now got the plan from a professional, why not?
sentences.zh: 如果你现在已经从专业人士那里得到了计划，想要自己去执行，那为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Why not go and do that yourself?
sentences.zh: 为什么不自己去试试呢？

sentences.en: Because if you can and you're comfortable doing it, then absolutely crack on.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你能做到，而且做起来很自在，那就尽管去做吧。

sentences.en: And I think the old transaction way was, we'll keep a hold of these relationships for as long as possible.
sentences.zh: 我认为过去那种交易式的方式是：尽可能长时间地维持这些关系。

sentences.en: And that world is changing, I think, over the next 10 or 50 years.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在未来10到50年里，那个世界正在改变。

sentences.en: It's going to be incredibly exciting because more and more people are starting to do this.
sentences.zh: 这将是非常令人兴奋的，因为越来越多的人开始尝试这样做。

sentences.en: And there's younger advisors coming in.
sentences.zh: 而且有更年轻的顾问加入进来。

sentences.en: I think the next evolution is going to be quite interesting for clients.
sentences.zh: 我认为下一次演变对客户来说会非常有趣。

sentences.en: Because it is risky.
sentences.zh: 因为这确实有风险。

sentences.en: It is risky.
sentences.zh: 确实有风险。

sentences.en: And it's that, you know, your funds may be at risk that feels, oh, it feels really scary, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 那种“你的资金可能面临风险”的感觉，哦，真的很吓人，不是吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, I definitely don't understand enough to be doing it myself.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我肯定没有足够的了解来自己操作。

sentences.en: I did have a little bit of a dabble in, like, an online share trading thing.
sentences.zh: 我确实稍微尝试过一点，比如在线股票交易之类的东西。

sentences.en: But I don't know what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And it's a small amount, enough amount.
sentences.zh: 那只是一小笔钱，数额不多。

sentences.en: It doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 其实没关系。

sentences.en: It doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 真的没关系。

sentences.en: But I definitely am not good enough to do this by myself for anything more than I have already.
sentences.zh: 但我绝对没有能力在现有基础上独自处理更多的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing is, like, you could have a dabble with this stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以尝试一下这些东西，对吧？

sentences.en: You could start off with a relatively small amount and say, well, if I put £100 into one of these accounts, forget about how much it is, but look at the percentage figures on it.
sentences.zh: 你可以从相对较小的金额开始，比如，如果我往这些账户里存了100英镑，先别管金额是多少，看看它的百分比数据。

sentences.en: So look at the percentage returns.
sentences.zh: 看看百分比收益率。

sentences.en: So if you're managing £100, because you need to be able to manage £100 to manage £1,000 to manage £100 to manage £100 to manage the million, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你能管理好100英镑，因为你需要有能力管理100英镑，才能管理1000英镑，才能管理10万，才能管理100万，对吧？

sentences.en: You've got to understand the fundamentals of that £100.
sentences.zh: 你必须理解那100英镑背后的基本原理。

sentences.en: But you could put that into an account and look at the percentages.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它存入账户，然后观察百分比变化。

sentences.en: And if that fund drops 20%, how would you feel if that was £100,000?
sentences.zh: 如果那笔基金下跌了20%，如果那是10万英镑，你会作何感想？

sentences.en: How would you feel if that was half a million, if that was your life savings?
sentences.zh: 如果那是50万英镑，如果那是你的毕生积蓄，你会感觉如何？

sentences.en: And if that is the kind of thing that worries you, then you need to get a professional involved.
sentences.zh: 如果这是让你担心的事情，那么你就需要专业人士介入。

sentences.en: If you're okay with those fluctuations, then potentially you could do it yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你能接受这些波动，那么你或许可以自己操作。

sentences.en: Now, playing around with £100 and actually being at the level where you're managing that yourself,
sentences.zh: 现在，拿着100英镑玩玩，和真正达到能自己管理资金的水平是两码事，

sentences.en: and you can have an impact on that return positively and negatively, you've almost got that extra layer of security with a financial advisor in there.
sentences.zh: 而且你可能会对回报产生正面或负面的影响，如果有理财顾问在场，你几乎就多了一层安全保障。

sentences.en: Because if you make the wrong decision and that drops yourself, how do you recover that?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你做出了错误的决定导致亏损，你该如何挽回？

sentences.en: And that tends to be the thing that happens.
sentences.zh: 这往往就是会发生的事情。

sentences.en: And I see it a lot over the years, like people that manage the funds themselves and there's some people out there who do a great job.
sentences.zh: 这些年来我见得很多，比如那些自己管理资金的人，确实有些人做得很好。

sentences.en: There's a tendency to overpanic.
sentences.zh: 但人们往往会过度恐慌。

sentences.en: So when markets go down, there's an overpanic of, crikey, it's dropped 20%.
sentences.zh: 所以当市场下跌时，人们会过度恐慌，心想：天哪，跌了20%。

sentences.en: What do I do?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么办？

sentences.en: Whereas if you take a step back, fund managers don't do anything.
sentences.zh: 而如果你退后一步看，基金经理们什么都不会做。

sentences.en: They'll just sit tight because they know it will come back.
sentences.zh: 他们只会按兵不动，因为他们知道市场会回升。

sentences.en: You can overtrade.
sentences.zh: 你可能会过度交易。

sentences.en: So you'll buy and sell more frequently, I guess, than I would if I was looking after it for you.
sentences.zh: 我想，比起我为你打理的情况，你会更频繁地买卖。

sentences.en: Because we're thinking three, five-year time horizon.
sentences.zh: 因为我们考虑的是三到五年的时间跨度。

sentences.en: Reset the clock, start again, and just kind of repeat over a period of time.
sentences.zh: 重置时钟，重新开始，然后在一段时间内重复这个过程。

sentences.en: If you're kind of buying and selling stocks and shares to try and make returns on an almost daily or weekly basis, that's incredibly risky.
sentences.zh: 如果你为了追求收益而几乎每天或每周都在买卖股票，那是非常危险的。

sentences.en: There was another one that's just gone.
sentences.zh: 刚才还漏掉了一点。

sentences.en: So it was the overtrade inside of things.
sentences.zh: 就是过度交易那一面。

sentences.en: It was the panic buying, the tendency to buy funds that you're really comfortable with or name brand names that you know, which is a good starting point.
sentences.zh: 还有恐慌性买入，倾向于购买你非常熟悉或你所知的品牌基金，这虽然是一个好的起点。

sentences.en: But actually, if you think about it, are those big companies going to continue that level of growth or do you want, like, the next Amazon, the next Apple?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果你仔细想想，那些大公司会继续保持那种增长水平吗？还是说你想要下一个亚马逊、下一个苹果？

sentences.en: Obviously, you want the next Amazon, the next Apple.
sentences.zh: 显然，你想要下一个亚马逊、下一个苹果。

sentences.en: But whereas if you're using a fund manager, they can potentially spot that because they've got teams of analysts and all that that sit behind that.
sentences.zh: 但如果你使用基金经理，他们可能能够发现这些机会，因为他们背后有分析师团队等等。

sentences.en: But it's a hard balancing act,
sentences.zh: 但这很难平衡，

sentences.en: but if you can start off relatively small and you're comfortable with it and you can almost multiply that out of the bigger numbers and you still feel comfortable with the 20% drop,
sentences.zh: 但如果你能从相对较小的金额开始，并且对此感到自在，几乎可以把这种感觉放大到更大的数字，而且你仍然能接受20%的跌幅，

sentences.en: give it a go.
sentences.zh: 那就试一试。

sentences.en: You might just need someone to give you a bit of a help along the way and reach out a financial advisor and say, what are you thinking of this?
sentences.zh: 你可能只是需要有人在过程中给你一点帮助，联系一位理财顾问，问问他们：你觉得这个怎么样？

sentences.en: Can I have a sense check on where I am?
sentences.zh: 我能对自己的现状做一个评估吗？

sentences.en: Is this going to be able to deliver me A, B, C, and D?
sentences.zh: 这能帮我实现A、B、C和D吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely, 100%.
sentences.zh: 当然，百分之百可以。

sentences.en: And there are advisors out there that will do that for you.
sentences.zh: 市面上确实有愿意为你做这些的顾问。

sentences.en: There are other advisors out there that will say, that's your bag, you crack on.
sentences.zh: 也有其他顾问会说，那是你的事，你自己去搞定吧。

sentences.en: You've got to find the right person to work with.
sentences.zh: 你必须找到合适的人合作。

sentences.en: Yeah, great advice.
sentences.zh: 是的，很好的建议。

sentences.en: And, you know, some advisors are independent and some are not.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有些顾问是独立的，有些则不是。

sentences.en: Is there a right or wrong approach there?
sentences.zh: 这其中有对错之分吗？

sentences.en: How would we even begin to understand why that's a good or bad thing?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何开始理解为什么这是好事或坏事？

sentences.en: The thing for me is you need to find an advisor that you truSt.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，你需要找到一个你信任的顾问。

sentences.en: And whether that advisor is on a restricted basis or completely independent, you need to find someone that you're comfortable with.
sentences.zh: 无论这位顾问是受限的还是完全独立的，你都需要找到一个让你感到自在的人。

sentences.en: If you want, find another one.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，可以再找一个。

sentences.en: And that could mean that there are people out there that I've had conversations with that didn't feel comfortable with me.
sentences.zh: 这意味着有些人曾与我交谈过，但觉得和我相处不自在。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: I'm not everybody's cup of tea and every financial advisor isn't going to be everybody's cup of tea.
sentences.zh: 我不是每个人的“那杯茶”，每个理财顾问也不可能适合所有人。

sentences.en: It's like get a second opinion.
sentences.zh: 就像寻求第二意见一样。

sentences.en: Find someone that you feel confident having those conversations with.
sentences.zh: 找一个让你有信心进行这些对话的人。

sentences.en: And when you do, stick with them.
sentences.zh: 一旦找到了，就坚持与他们合作。

sentences.en: Whether they are restricted, which means they'll work from a certain panel of providers or they might only work with one internal set of funds.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是受限的（意味着他们只从特定的供应商名单中选择，或者可能只使用内部的一套基金），

sentences.en: Or whether they're independent, which is the whole of market.
sentences.zh: 还是独立的（即全市场选择）。

sentences.en: And I've done both of them.
sentences.zh: 这两种我都做过。

sentences.en: I'm now completely independent.
sentences.zh: 我现在是完全独立的。

sentences.en: And I just felt like I was at the stage of my career where I wanted more, I guess, options and alternatives to what was available out there.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得我处于职业生涯的这个阶段，我想要更多的选择和替代方案，而不是仅仅局限于现有的东西。

sentences.en: And to be able to fully utilize my 17 years of experience to deliver the best possible outcomes for clients.
sentences.zh: 并且能够充分利用我17年的经验，为客户提供尽可能最好的结果。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that if you're with a restricted advisor, they're not going to give you the best possible outcome.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着如果你选择了一位受限的顾问，他们就无法给你最好的结果。

sentences.en: Because if they're looking after you properly and they are managing everything properly for you, then why rock the boat?
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们妥善地照顾你，并且为你妥善管理一切，那么为什么要折腾呢？

sentences.en: I think a lot of the time you can get all caught up in returns.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多时候人们会陷入对收益的纠结中。

sentences.en: But if you're with somebody who makes you feel safe, secure, and you're having the right kind of conversations with them,
sentences.zh: 但如果你和某人在一起，让你感到安全、有保障，并且你们之间有正确的对话，

sentences.en: whether they're restricted or independent doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是受限的还是独立的，其实并不重要。

sentences.en: If you're just looking from a, I want as many possible options as possible, independent has to be the way to go because you've got the whole of the market available.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是从“我想要尽可能多的选择”的角度来看，独立顾问确实是必经之路，因为你可以利用整个市场。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean it's right for everybody.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它适合所有人。

sentences.en: It's about finding the advisor first and then understanding what they can offer.
sentences.zh: 关键是先找到顾问，然后了解他们能提供什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think it's like getting any job done in your house.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就像在家里做任何工作一样。

sentences.en: You should get at least three quotes, shouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 你应该至少获得三份报价，不是吗？

sentences.en: You should have three meetings with three different advisors.
sentences.zh: 你应该和三位不同的顾问进行三次会面。

sentences.en: And then maybe also try and do a bit of your research yourself to try and get your own kind of sense of what is available and how it compares.
sentences.zh: 然后也许还可以尝试自己做一点研究，试着对市场上的选择以及它们如何比较有一个自己的判断。

sentences.en: And if it doesn't feel right, don't do it.
sentences.zh: 如果感觉不对，就不要做。

sentences.en: Like, even if you have those three meetings, I had someone a couple of years back who I was the seventh advisor that he'd spoken to in a row
sentences.zh: 即使你进行了那三次会面，几年前我遇到过一个人，我是他连续交谈过的第七位顾问，

sentences.en: because he just wasn't sure who he was going to pick, what kind of style he wanted,
sentences.zh: 因为他不确定该选谁，也不确定自己想要什么样的风格，

sentences.en: because we all operate in slightly different ways, depending on what our experience is, what our qualifications are.
sentences.zh: 因为我们每个人的运作方式略有不同，取决于我们的经验和资质。

sentences.en: You'll get a different experience from each advisor, but ultimately he ended up picking me because it was a very different approach.
sentences.zh: 你会从每位顾问那里得到不同的体验，但他最终选择了我，因为我的方法非常不同。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean my approach will work for you.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我的方法适合你。

sentences.en: You might want the transactional stuff.
sentences.zh: 你可能想要那种交易式的服务。

sentences.en: You might want to go through the process and just be really hands-off, tell me what I need to do.
sentences.zh: 你可能想走完流程，然后完全当甩手掌柜，告诉我就行了。

sentences.en: And everybody's different.
sentences.zh: 每个人都是不同的。

sentences.en: Have those conversations.
sentences.zh: 去进行那些对话吧。

sentences.en: And if it doesn't feel right after three, then have four, maybe have five, have six.
sentences.zh: 如果三次之后感觉不对，那就再找第四个，也许第五个、第六个。

sentences.en: If it doesn't feel right, then actually, is financial advice right for you?
sentences.zh: 如果还是感觉不对，那么，理财咨询真的适合你吗？

sentences.en: Do you need to just take a step back for a moment and think, well, just because everybody's getting financial advice doesn't mean it's the right thing for you right now.
sentences.zh: 你是否需要退后一步，想一想：仅仅因为每个人都在接受理财咨询，并不意味着它现在就适合你。

sentences.en: I'm a firm believer that everybody should have access to a financial advisor at some point.
sentences.zh: 我坚信每个人在某个阶段都应该有机会接触理财顾问。

sentences.en: It might not be the right point in time for you to have access to them.
sentences.zh: 但现在可能并不是你接触他们的最佳时机。

sentences.en: Then you might just need a bit of a nudge in the right direction from a friend or a relative.
sentences.zh: 那么你可能只需要朋友或亲戚的一点点指引。

sentences.en: Have those conversations and it's the old stiff British upper lip, isn't it, that we don't talk about money because it's rude and crass.
sentences.zh: 去进行那些对话吧，那种英国人传统的“咬紧牙关”的作风，认为谈钱粗俗无礼，不是吗？

sentences.en: For me, that's nonsense.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是胡说八道。

sentences.en: Have the conversations with people that you know because they'll have made some of the mistakes that you are.
sentences.zh: 和认识的人交谈，因为他们可能犯过你正在犯的一些错误。

sentences.en: You're not going to be asking them exactly what they invest in.
sentences.zh: 你不需要问他们具体投资了什么。

sentences.en: Just be like, do you mind just telling me a little bit about what you do with your money?
sentences.zh: 只要说：你介意跟我聊聊你是怎么处理钱的吗？

sentences.en: I don't want to know figures or anything.
sentences.zh: 我不想知道具体数字之类的。

sentences.en: What do you do?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做的？

sentences.en: How do you do it?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么操作的？

sentences.en: Because you'll get different ideas and everyone's going to have a different opinion.
sentences.zh: 因为你会得到不同的想法，每个人都会有不同的意见。

sentences.en: I guess the other caveat I've got to add to that is that's not Bob the Pisshead down the pub who's never got any money because you're always buying him a beer.
sentences.zh: 我想我必须补充的另一个注意事项是，那不是指酒吧里那个总是没钱、因为你一直在请他喝酒的酒鬼鲍勃。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at that logically, he's probably not great with money, but people that you know are okay with money are okay financially.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你逻辑地看，他可能不擅长理财，但你认识的那些理财状况良好的人，他们的财务状况是没问题的。

sentences.en: Have those conversations.
sentences.zh: 去进行那些对话吧。

sentences.en: Bob the Pisshead down the pub might be richer than anybody because he doesn't spend his own money.
sentences.zh: 酒吧里的酒鬼鲍勃可能比任何人都富有，因为他从不花自己的钱。

sentences.en: You never know.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: You never know.
sentences.zh: 你永远不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, it's unlikely, but it's possible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不太可能，但确实有可能。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: And, you know, someone who's in their early 20s, perhaps listening to this,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，一个20出头的人，也许正在听这个，

sentences.en: how can they even begin to fathom what they might need and what the cost of living situation is going to be by the time they get to be in their late 60s, early 70s?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么能开始设想自己需要什么，以及等到他们60多岁、70多岁时生活成本会是什么样？

sentences.en: Probably by the time they get to retire, it might even be 80s.
sentences.zh: 可能等到他们退休时，甚至可能是80多岁了。

sentences.en: How can they begin to imagine and work that out, what they might need?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么能开始想象并计算出他们可能需要什么呢？

sentences.en: It's tough.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: It's really, really tough.
sentences.zh: 真的非常非常难。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: and if you look at like generationally where we are and how difficult it is for us to get onto the property that like my kids and certainly your kids will find it even harder than we did to get onto that property ladder.
sentences.zh: 如果你从代际的角度看看我们现在的处境，看看我们想要置业有多么困难，你就会发现，我的孩子们，当然还有你的孩子们，想要踏上这级置业阶梯会比我们更加艰难。

sentences.en: And are they going to be able to do that without parental support, without parental help?
sentences.zh: 那么，没有父母的支持和帮助，他们能做到吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: And that's the hard bit.
sentences.zh: 而这正是最困难的部分。

sentences.en: That's the moving part that we just can't predict.
sentences.zh: 这是我们无法预测的变数。

sentences.en: But what I encourage you to do is, if you're in that position, is to just try and also map out like ultimately dream blue sky scenario.
sentences.zh: 但我鼓励你，如果你正处于那种境地，试着去规划一下，描绘出你心中最理想的蓝图。

sentences.en: What do you want your retirement and your end goal to look like?
sentences.zh: 你希望你的退休生活和最终目标是什么样的？

sentences.en: And this is what I talk to clients about.
sentences.zh: 这也是我和客户谈论的内容。

sentences.en: And it's that North Star in the sky of if everything fell into place and everything happened exactly the way I wanted, which it won't, by the way,
sentences.zh: 这就是你心中的那颗北极星，如果一切都如你所愿地顺遂发展——当然，现实中不会完全如此——

sentences.en: what do you want your retirement to look like?
sentences.zh: 你希望你的退休生活是什么样的？

sentences.en: Is that going to be like your grandparents?
sentences.zh: 是像你祖父母那样吗？

sentences.en: Is it going to be like your parents?
sentences.zh: 是像你父母那样吗？

sentences.en: Is it going to be like your Uncle Bob?
sentences.zh: 还是像你鲍勃叔叔那样？

sentences.en: Whoever it is, try and paint that picture a little bit.
sentences.zh: 无论那个人是谁，试着去勾勒出那幅画面。

sentences.en: And if you can paint that picture, then you could almost reverse engineer that right the way back to where you are now.
sentences.zh: 如果你能勾勒出那幅画面，你几乎可以从现在的位置开始进行逆向推导。

sentences.en: And it might be that you can't do that.
sentences.zh: 也许你现在还做不到。

sentences.en: And it might be that all you can think about is the next five years.
sentences.zh: 也许你目前只能想到未来五年。

sentences.en: And that next five years might be, I want to get on the property ladder.
sentences.zh: 而这未来五年可能是：我想踏上置业阶梯。

sentences.en: I want to make sure I've got some savings behind me in case the shit hits the fan, washing machine breaks down or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 我想确保自己有一些积蓄，以防万一遇到突发状况，比如洗衣机坏了之类的琐事。

sentences.en: I want to be able to afford to put the kids into nursery because I plan to go back to school.
sentences.zh: 我想有能力负担得起送孩子去托儿所的费用，因为我打算重返校园。

sentences.en: Just figure that out and talk that through.
sentences.zh: 把这些理清楚，并谈论出来。

sentences.en: If you've got a partner I do that with, amazing.
sentences.zh: 如果你有伴侣可以一起商量，那太棒了。

sentences.en: If you've got friends you can have that conversation with,
sentences.zh: 如果你有朋友可以进行这种交流，

sentences.en: great because certainly what I found is having those things in your head is very different to writing them down on a sheet of paper or very different to verbalizing them because they sound very differently and resonate on a different level.
sentences.zh: 那也很好，因为我确实发现，把这些想法放在脑子里和把它们写在纸上，或者说出来，是完全不同的，因为它们听起来感觉不同，产生的共鸣层面也不同。

sentences.en: And if it is just a five-year plan of I want to get on the property ladder or I want to move out of the family home or whatever it might be,
sentences.zh: 如果这只是一个五年计划，比如我想买房，或者想搬出原生家庭，无论是什么，

sentences.en: then try and figure out what that looks like.
sentences.zh: 那就试着弄清楚它是什么样子的。

sentences.en: You don't have to do it all at once.
sentences.zh: 你不必一次性完成所有事情。

sentences.en: Like if we all did it all at once and we all kind of in our 20s knew exactly what we were going to do for the rest of our lives, we'd all be retired at 55.
sentences.zh: 如果我们都在二十多岁时就一次性规划好余生，那我们所有人都能在55岁退休了。

sentences.en: You'd all be retired at 50 and you'd all have a great old life and the poverty wouldn't exist and all these other kind of horrible things that are out there because we'd all have our,
sentences.zh: 你们都能在50岁退休，过上美好的生活，贫困也不会存在，那些可怕的事情也不会发生，因为我们都……

sentences.en: I nearly swore again, we'd all have everything together and know exactly the direction we're going.
sentences.zh: 我差点又说脏话了，因为我们都能把一切打理得井井有条，明确知道自己前进的方向。

sentences.en: And that's impossible.
sentences.zh: 但这是不可能的。

sentences.en: But sometimes it's just figure out maybe the five-year plan and then the next step and the one after that and the one after that and the one after that.
sentences.zh: 但有时只需要先制定个五年计划，然后是下一步，再下一步，以此类推。

sentences.en: And that's what I tell clients, we'll figure out what the long-term really important stuff is and why that's important to you.
sentences.zh: 这就是我告诉客户的，我们会找出长期来看真正重要的事情，以及为什么它们对你很重要。

sentences.en: We'll try and reverse engineer that and if we can't,
sentences.zh: 我们会尝试进行逆向推导，如果做不到，

sentences.en: we'll just figure out what we're going to do tomorrow and then what we're going to do next week and we're going to do next month, next six months, next year.
sentences.zh: 我们就先弄清楚明天要做什么，然后是下周、下个月、未来六个月、未来一年要做什么。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, two, three years in and you've got that plan that starts to kind of fall into place.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，两三年过去了，你就会发现那个计划开始逐渐成形了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's tricky, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是啊，这确实很棘手，不是吗？

sentences.en: Like, this is, I guess, where dream boards and vision boards and Pinterest come in that you can dare to imagine what you might want your life to look like.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是梦想板、愿景板和Pinterest派上用场的地方，你可以大胆想象你想要的生活是什么样的。

sentences.en: And that's not suggesting, you know, we don't need to be disloyal to the life we're living now.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说我们要背叛现在的生活。
